Prayer for the Return of the Captives, by Rabbi David Lau (Office of the Ashkenazi Chief Rabbi of Israel 2024)

tei:availability.tei:p: Edict of government (Compendium II, Copyright Office Practices, §206.01)

tei:div.tei:head: Prayer for the Return of the Captives, by Rabbi David Lau (Office of the Ashkenazi Chief Rabbi of Israel 2024)

tei:lg.tei:l: May it be the will of our Father in Heaven
Who brought His people Israel out from the suffering of Egypt
that He bless and save our abducted brothers and sisters,
May He strengthen their souls and faith,
Protect them from all harm and disease,
Have mercy on His sons and daughters awaiting His salvation,
Nullify all cruel decrees from upon them.
and may they quickly emerge from darkness to light,
and from the pit of captivity to the freedom of the world,
and return in peace to their families and to their homes.
Please, plant brotherhood, peace and friendship in the hearts of all,
and spread over us the Sukkah of Your peace,
And may we merit to soon sing before You a ‘New Song.’

tei:note.tei:p: The shir ḥadash or shirah ḥadashah (“new song”) is a motif found in numerous psalms and in Isaiah 42:10. In rabbinic Judaism the motif has a powerful messianic resonance, signifying liberation, the end of the Galut, and the realization of a new messianic age. The phrase is invoked at the opening of the first portion of Hallel (Psalms 113 and 114) in the Maggid section of the Passover seder haggadah as well as at the very end of the formula of the second blessing over the wine (concluding Maggid). –ANV
